items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: That's one thing I used to like about Duke's band, when Sonny Greer was in the band.

ctx.x: Well, now, would you say you were inspired by this kind of a rhythm section?

Oh, I loved it. Yes, indeed. Paul Barbarin. Boy, he... Nothin' flashy about it. But see, with a rhythm section, you're not supposed to hear it... Like drums and all of this technique... You're not supposed to hear the rhythm section. You're supposed to feel it. You're supposed to feel that rhythm. You're not supposed to hear it, a whole lot of bangin' and this-that-and-the-other. That's not a rhythm section. But it's supposed to inspire you, make you want to dance or do something, make you pat your feet, do…

That's one thing I used to like about Duke's band, when Sonny Greer was in the band. Sonny was never acclaimed to be what you call a real star drummer, you know. But when he was with Duke's band, I don't care what other drummer Duke had or used in his band. None of them fit in the band like Sonny Greer did. Sonny had an old-fashioned beat, [SINGS IT], real jungle effect music. And it fit right into Duke's band. It just fit there. And when Sonny left the band, Duke tried out a whole lot of drummers, a whole lot of…

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Then they come up with another fellow named Sonny something-or-other, but he didn't last either... I was out of the band this time -- I was gone again.

ctx.x: Now, you mentioned everybody wanted to be a leader in that band, and they had many different people fronting the band.

Yeah, they had a lot of different leaders in front of the band. They started off with Carroll Dickerson from Chicago. He was the first leader, I think, in front of the band. Then they come up with another fellow named Sonny something-or-other, but he didn't last either... Q: Sonny Adams? You mentioned Sonny Adams. Was that the name?

No. Sonny Adams was a tenor player. But this leader's name was Sonny something. Well, anyway, then they had Baron Lee; he was the third leader that I know of. And after that, I don't know, because I was out of the band this time -- I was gone again. Then I think Lucky Millinder was about the last one that was in front of the band. It was still the Blue Rhythm Band when Lucky Millinder taken it over.
